video.title: Rockstar Just WENT AFTER Grand Theft Auto 6 MODDING and PC!

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Rant: PC players always get the short end of the stick from Rockstar; PC has grown enormously since GTA V yet GTA 6 ships day one on Xbox, a much smaller market. Hook is the 'short end of the stick' claim (open on 'For a myriad of reasons', dropping 'However'). Payoff: 'You guys are gonna have it on Xbox. You can get a PC version ready.' Two endings genuinely work: that line (preferred, ~46s), or running on through 'they've never wanted to do it' and the GTA V / Red Dead 2 / GTA 4 / LA Noire list at 122.0, which caps it but is mostly a second pass.

Hot take: by skipping PC, Rockstar hands Sony a free pseudo-exclusive in GTA 6, since Xbox is irrelevant. Hook: 'what I hate more than anything...' Payoff: 'I don't think PlayStation's paying whatsoever... it's gonna come out regardless, just because they're not releasing the game on PC.' Shortest landing is 'handing PlayStation a free exclusive' (552.8). What follows (Xbox irrelevant, 'pushes PS5 consoles') restates.

Prediction played for a laugh: once GTA 6 is out there will be tweets and think pieces calling it overrated, because hype this big can never be met. Hook: 'I am also fully convinced...' Punchline: 'Even if it's the greatest game of all time, bro, it's not gonna fix your personal life. I'm sorry to say, it's a video game.' ~31s.

also_ok.why: Rockstar's new mod rules ban fan storylines; Mush pushes back: who cares, it's not canon, and modded players are a drop in the bucket. Needs the rule read out as setup (opens on 'as noted on GameRant, Rockstar splits its new mod guidelines...'), so it's half narration of an article; acceptable, not essential. Ends on 'it's not canon' (207.1) or runs to 'drop in the bucket' / 'protective of their IP' (230.7).

negatives.why: Intro run-up: 'the general consensus... some of the best games in the history of gaming' sounds like a strong claim but only sets up the actual topic; no payoff.
Reading sections two and three of the mod guidelines off the article, with brief 'is that the biggest deal?' asides; screen narration.
Fourth-section monetization rule plus a quick 'that's when the game changes' reaction; opens on a list reference and the reaction is thin.
Rambling on whether Rockstar can enforce the rules against IP-crossover mods; no point lands, and it trails into the PC release topic.
